newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso closes at record-low vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso closes at record-low vs dollar.

text.p: Colombia's peso closed at a record-low of 1,074.90 against the dollar after a day of active trading on the country's interbank market marked by strong demand for U.S. currency, dealers said.
They said demand for greenbacks came from the corporate and banking sectors alike and was fueled by widespread expectations that the peso will continue it downward trend in the days and weeks ahead.
"There's a lot of speculation because of forecasts about a greater devaluation," said one currency trader.
He and others said automotive assembly plants were among the biggest buyers of dollars, moving en masse to stock up on cash for sorely needed imports before the peso headed further south.
Sporadic dollars sales, including some by state-owned exporters, failed to offer the peso any support, traders said.
They said Monday's close was the lowest since June 3 of last year, when the peso ended at 1,074.85, and had set a new record versus the dollar.
Dealers reported a hectic 471 trades for $212 million and said the peso moved from an intraday low of 1,054.50 to 1,075 before the close.
Expectations of an imminent cut in domestic interest rates added to the run on dollars, the dealers said. ((-- Juan Guillermo Londono, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944))
